first_sentence: The denominator is every control the entry's own deliverables name, parsed from four documents a judge already holds. A control in this repository's code is probed or it is listed by name as unprobed with the reason; only a control that lives outside the code is out of scope, and the page says where it lives. Nothing is dropped, so the count cannot be improved by choosing less, and no ratio is published.

entries.statement: 14/14 and 12/12 held. Four were found by red-teaming our own fixes: an agent could approve its own card (the rule lived at the HTTP perimeter, which a compromised agent bypasses), one token authorised unlimited executions, a concurrent race defeated the single-use fix (12 threads, 5 writes from one approval), and re-registering a decided card erased a deny-by-default and re-minted its token
probes: card must be APPROVED check removed

entries.statement: 11 pass. A hash chain cannot detect TRUNCATION, and a reviewer removed the last four events with `verify()` still returning ok. Every append now writes a MAC'd head anchor; a shortened chain reports how many events are missing. Both peppers are source literals, so this raises the bar from deleting lines to forging a MAC and a root adversary still wins, which is why the word is tamper-evident

passes. Approval state uses an exclusive flock across every read-modify-write with atomic rename; the lock sentinel lives outside the checkout, because `reset()` deleting it broke mutual exclusion for a concurrent holder. Ledger appends serialise in both implementations across threads and, since 2026-08-26, across processes: the thread lock could not see the console server and `agentcore/replay.py --keep-state` writing one console ledger from two processes, which forks the chain. Both implementations now hold an exclusive flock, keyed by the ledger path and kept outside the checkout, across the tip read, the event write and the head-anchor rewrite, and the stub re-validates its chain-tip cache under that lock. The process case is pinned by `agentcore/tests/test_ledger_append_shared.py` and `governance/tests/test_ledger_shared.py` (`python -m pytest agentcore/tests/test_ledger_append_shared.py governance/tests/test_ledger_shared.py -q`): each starts two OS processes on a barrier that append 300 events apiece to one file, and with the file lock removed both fail 5 of 5 runs with `event 1: prev_hash mismatch` on a 600-event file
